name: kaldrax-memory-extraction-v1
description: Annotated synthetic engineering candidates. Expected claims have manually authored match_terms used for deterministic one-to-one matching; confidence metrics are descriptive for this sample only.

cases.candidate: Decision: SQLite is the local durable store. The database uses write-ahead logging and a busy timeout. Rule: schema upgrades are additive and preserve existing rows. A developer also prefers dark terminal themes.
Rule: retryable writes require idempotency keys. API throttling returns Retry-After. Decision: list endpoints use opaque cursors so pagination remains stable while records change.

cases.objective: Extract security controls from implementation notes
cases.candidate: Rule: session cookies use Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite. Rule: credentials and authorization headers are redacted from logs. Rule: database access uses parameterized SQL rather than string interpolation.

Pattern: the outbox row is committed in the same transaction as the domain update. Rule: transient failures use exponential backoff with jitter. Rule: exhausted messages move to a dead-letter queue with the failure reason preserved.

Rule: structured logs include a correlation identifier and redact personal data. Rule: trace identifiers propagate into background jobs. Decision: alert on service-level objective burn rate rather than host CPU alone.

Rule: readiness checks fail when a required dependency is unavailable. Rule: a failed post-deploy health check triggers rollback to the previous artifact. CI pins the Python runtime and uses the dependency lock file.
Rule: all interactive controls work with keyboard navigation and show visible focus. Rule: text meets WCAG AA contrast requirements. Status must not be communicated by color alone.

Pattern: property-based tests exercise parser invariants over generated inputs. Rule: migration tests include the oldest supported database schema. CI runs formatting, lint, type checking, and static analysis.
Rule: restore drills verify that backups are recoverable. Rule: risky launches use feature flags with an emergency kill switch. Rule: service containers run as a non-root user.

cases.objective: Extract architectural boundaries and configuration safety
cases.candidate: Decision: domain workflows depend on stable ports while provider integrations remain replaceable adapters. Rule: all memory reads are isolated by project identifier. Rule: required configuration is type-checked at startup and errors do not reveal secret values.
